name: Bontari House Rules: Altered Official Items

text.content:
Nerf, Buff, or Side-Grade: SIDE-GRADE/UPGRADE
Reasoning: According to James Hutt, one of designers of the game, has stated that the reason Big Knucks/Gorilla Arms count as melee weapons is so they can ignore half of the target's armor. So this change just applies that same rule to Brawling attacks made with them, because it doesn't really make sense for it not to be Brawling.

Instead of being counted as a Melee weapon Gorilla Arms now allow your Brawling attacks to ignore half armor. This means you now use Brawling instead of Melee Weapon skill when making attacks. In addition, having two Gorilla Arms counts as having 11 BODY for the purpose of determining Brawling/Martial Arts damage (making it 4d6).

Foundry notes:

  • Cyberpunk RED - Core has no Gorilla Arms item. Corgo's 77 Collection has its own Gorilla Arm, which already uses Brawling.

From Bontari Homebrew Cyberpunk Items by Bontari (OFFICIAL ITEMS WITH ALTERED RUL).

Nerf, Buff, or Side-Grade: SIDE-GRADE/NERF
Reasoning: Neuroports replace the utility of Agents in cases, however Agents still have a role in game for non-cybernetic individuals or people who want a secondary line of communication. These changes are meant to integrate Agents into the Edgerunners Mission Kit's rules for quickhacks and the new role Netrunners play.

Agents are effectively smartphones. Common among Nomads and Luddites to substitute the main functions of a Neuroport. Agents can be quickhacked like Neuroports, with damage dealt affecting the Agent. All Agents have 5 HP and are Destroyed when reduced to 0 HP. When Jacking In to an Agent with Interface you skip the initial roll to avoid detection (unless the Agent is actively being used). By default the NetArc of an Agent is a single Control Node floor just like a Neuroport.

Agents no longer provide a +2 to Library Search. Instead Library Search rolls take a -2 penalty when made without either an Agent or Neuroport. It's now standard to have an always accessable internet device.

The DV of the Control Node is determined by the quality of the Agent. Most common Agent brands are Raven Microtechnics, Rocklin, and Zetatech.

Standard (100eb, DV 8 Control Node)
Excellent (500eb, DV 10 Control Node)

Foundry notes:

  • Built as Agent, Standard (Bontari Edition) and Agent, Excellent (Bontari Edition) in the Bontari Editions compendium.

From Bontari Homebrew Cyberpunk Items by Bontari (OFFICIAL ITEMS WITH ALTERED RUL).

Nerf, Buff, or Side-Grade: UPGRADE
Reasoning: Cyberfingers are extremely minor pieces of cyberware that are not worth having using normal max humanity depression rules. So instead explicitly adding few but more patentially impactful spots.

Individual cyberfiger cyberware isn't availible. Instead You have two cyberhand slots.
